page_title: “Offline First” with Service Worker (Building a PWA, Part 1)

summary.title: "Offline First" with Service Worker (Building a PWA, Part 1)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to precache an app shell with a Service Worker (using the sw-toolbox library) and serve cached files offline in a plain-JavaScript progressive web app.
keywords: udacity senior web developer nanodegree capstone
takeaways: The app shell model caches the static parts of a page (HTML, CSS, JS) so they load instantly on repeat visits.
A manual Service Worker precache needs install and activate handlers plus versioned cache cleanup.
Google's sw-toolbox lets you precache by passing an array of files to toolbox.precache().
In the fetch event, check the cache first with caches.match() and fall back to the network with fetch().
Cached files can be verified in Chrome under Developer Tools > Application > Cache Storage.
summary.summary: The author, building a capstone progressive web app for their blog in plain JavaScript (Gulp, Handlebars, SASS, Babel, Firebase hosting), explains the first half of an offline-first design: caching the app shell. The article contrasts a manual Service Worker precache (install/activate handlers and cache versioning) with the simpler Service Worker Toolbox precache API. It then shows a fetch handler that serves cached responses and falls back to the network, in both expanded and one-line ES2015 forms. It notes Google's newer sw-precache library as an alternative and says the next part covers IndexedDB for dynamic article data.
